title: The Elder Scrolls
subtitle: Arena to Skyrim in release order, expansions included
blurb: 5 mainline games, 5 expansions and 3 asides — about 286 hours of story, 163 of it the mainline.
paceLabel: the expansions, the detours and Online
notes: Every Elder Scrolls is a fresh province and a fresh nobody — nothing requires anything else, and starting at Morrowind or Skyrim is a long tradition. This is the release order, with the early pair kept honest rather than mandatory.

The five HowLongToBeat tracks as separate entries — Tribunal, Bloodmoon, Shivering Isles, Dawnguard, Dragonborn — each optional, each with its own hours. Smaller add-ons like Knights of the Nine ride along inside the modern editions and are not split out.
The 2025 Oblivion Remastered is the same story in better clothes; whichever edition you play, tick the one Oblivion row. Skyrim's many re-releases work the same way.
The Elder Scrolls Online is an MMO with no ending; its row carries HLTB's base-story figure and stays out of the finish-date maths.
HowLongToBeat main-story figures — the critical path through games famous for ignoring it. Treat every number as a floor.
Game list and years from Wikipedia's Elder Scrolls articles; hours from HowLongToBeat main-story figures, matched by name and year.
